paper: Chan AP, Choi Y, Brinkac LM, et al. (2020) AbGRI4, a novel antibiotic resistance island in multiply antibiotic-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates. J Antimicrob Chemother 75(10):2760-2768. doi:10.1093/jac/dkaa266. PMID:32681170. PMC7556812.

open_questions.q: Is the AbGRI4 island truly novel with respect to all previously described Acinetobacter baumannii class-1-integron resistance islands (AbGRI1/2/3 and related), or is it a re-observation / near-variant of an existing structure that had been catalogued under a different name?
open_questions.basis: The paper's central claim is novelty ('a novel antibiotic resistance island'), grounded in the specific aadB/aadA2/sul1 cassette in a class-1 integron chassis. This replication only verified that the marker triad is present in the correct three isolates; we did NOT re-execute a systematic search of A. baumannii public genomes for that exact cassette + integrase + insertion-site combination, and we did NOT compare against the full catalogue of previously published AbGRI/AbaR structures at base-pair resolution. Novelty is an assertion about the reference set, not just the observed set.
next_steps: Extract the full AbGRI4 island sequence (integrase intI1, attC sites, gene cassettes, IS flanking, terminal repeats) from each AbGRI4+ assembly using annotation (Bakta or Prokka) + manual curation of the class-1 integron boundaries.
BLASTn the island sequence against (a) NCBI nt limited to A. baumannii, (b) a curated resistance-island reference set (AbGRI1a/b, AbGRI2, AbGRI3, AbaR1-25, RESFINDERFG), and (c) ISfinder / INTEGRALL.

Report the top hits with %identity and %coverage. If any prior A. baumannii genome carries the identical cassette + integron in the same insertion context, downgrade 'novel' to 'reobserved-under-new-name' and flag for correction.

open_questions.q: Is AbGRI4 chromosomally integrated or plasmid-borne in each of ABUH763, ABUH793, ABUH796, and does its mobility differ across the three?
open_questions.basis: Rerun-side PlasmidFinder returned zero hits, but this is a known DB gap (PlasmidFinder's DB is Enterobacteriaceae-biased and does not represent Acinetobacter rep types). The absence of PlasmidFinder hits therefore does NOT constitute evidence for chromosomal location. Whether AbGRI4 sits on the chromosome or on an Acinetobacter-native plasmid materially changes the mobility and outbreak-transmission implications, and this was not directly re-adjudicated here.
next_steps: Identify the replicon each AbGRI4 sits on by locating the island in the finished assembly and confirming whether it is on the main chromosomal contig or on a separate plasmid contig (contig length + circularity + coverage should discriminate).
Run an Acinetobacter-appropriate plasmid-replicon caller (e.g. MOB-suite for mobility typing, Kaptive for K/O locus context, PLSDB BLASTn) rather than PlasmidFinder.
If plasmid-borne, extract the plasmid sequence and compare across the three AbGRI4+ isolates: identical plasmid = single-mobility event; divergent plasmids = independent acquisitions.

open_questions.q: Does the AbGRI4 genotype fully explain the aminoglycoside + sulfonamide susceptibility phenotypes reported in Chan et al., or are there phenotype-genotype mismatches that would indicate additional resistance mechanisms (e.g. efflux, target modification, uncalled genes)?
open_questions.basis: This replication verified the AbGRI4 gene content but did not re-generate MIC data or systematically cross-check phenotype vs. genotype across all 4 isolates and all reported antibiotic classes. A meaningful fraction of A. baumannii resistance is not accounted for by ABRicate-catchable acquired genes (overexpression of AdeABC, PBP mutations, LPS modification for polymyxin, etc.), so the paper's phenotype narrative is not fully audited by a gene-presence rerun.
next_steps: Extract the reported per-isolate MIC / susceptibility table from Chan et al. supplementary material.

For each isolate x antibiotic cell, cross-check against (a) the ABRicate calls in data/abricate/*.tsv and (b) point mutations in gyrA/parC (fluoroquinolone), pmrAB/lpxACD (colistin), and rpoB (rifampicin) using a variant-calling pass on the assemblies.
Report explicit concordance/discordance table; any discordant cell needs a mechanistic hypothesis (efflux upregulation, insertion sequence disruption, etc.).

open_questions.q: Are the four ABUH strains truly independent clinical isolates, or do genomic distances indicate they represent a hospital outbreak clone (i.e. one recent transmission event with subsequent divergence)?
open_questions.basis: All four isolates are ST2 (Pasteur), Cleveland OH, 2015 -- geographically and temporally clustered. If they are outbreak-related, the AbGRI4 presence/absence pattern could reflect a single loss-of-island event within a clone rather than three independent acquisitions plus one non-acquisition, which changes the interpretation of 'novel island distribution'. This replication did not compute a core-genome SNP distance matrix among the four ABUHs, which is the standard test for outbreak relatedness.
next_steps: Build a core-genome SNP alignment across the four ABUH assemblies using Snippy (or Roary + core alignment) against a common reference (e.g. A320 or one of the ABUHs as internal reference).
Compute pairwise SNP distances. Standard thresholds: <10 SNPs = strongly outbreak-related; 10-100 SNPs = likely related; >100 SNPs = distinct introductions.
If <100 SNPs across the four, rerun the AbGRI4 gain/loss inference: is it more parsimonious to explain the pattern as ancestral-present + loss-in-773, or as three independent gains?

open_questions.q: Do the AbGRI4+ isolates carry the AbGRI4 integron at the SAME chromosomal (or plasmid) insertion site, and does the local synteny support a single evolutionary origin of the island in this clone?
open_questions.basis: 'Same island' at the gene-content level (aadB/aadA2/sul1) does not imply 'same insertion event'. Three isolates could each carry an AbGRI4-like integron at different genomic locations, which would substantially change the mobility and evolutionary narrative. This replication verified gene presence, not synteny, insertion-site homology, or terminal-repeat identity.
next_steps: Extract 20-50 kb of flanking sequence around each AbGRI4 integron in the three AbGRI4+ assemblies.
Perform pairwise nucleotide alignment (nucmer or minimap2-asm) of the flanking regions to check for shared insertion context, direct repeats of the target-site duplication, and IS element boundaries.

If insertion sites and TSDs are identical: single origin, vertical inheritance in the clone. If divergent: independent horizontal acquisitions -- possibly with a common source but distinct integration events. Either result substantiates or refines the paper's mobility narrative.
